thread:
ada: Quick design thread: RFC follow-up on compact headers. We debated async enrich + join vs doing an append-only billing ledger at ingest time. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and an initial decision direction.

leo: TL;DR what is "billing ledger" option?

ada: Idea: instead of joining enriched attrs back into trace events, emit a small, append-only billing record at ingest time (from gateway) keyed by trace_id. The gateway creates the record by doing a tiny auth'd lookup (fast cache) for billing_key/customer. That record is the authoritative source for cost aggregation, separate from the main trace envelope.

neha: So gateway must sometimes do a sync lookup (or rely on local cache) to create ledger rows for billing routes. That reintroduces some sync latency but avoids later expensive joins/backfills.

sanjay: Pros I see: simpler billing queries (scan ledger), deterministic cost accounting, avoids late-attr window complexity. Cons: extra write per request and potential duplication if requests replay.

ada: Exactly. Draft ledger schema (tiny):
```
{ trace_id, billing_key, customer_id, route_id, ts, ledger_version, signature }
```
ledger rows are small (~120 bytes). We append to ledger stream which is optimized for fanout to billing rollups.

leo: How do we ensure idempotency? replayed requests could double-count.

neha: Include signature = HMAC(route_token || trace_id || ts) and ledger_version. Ledger consumer dedupes by trace_id + ledger_version; gateway increments version on retry. Also ledger ingestion checks for duplicate trace_id within a small window.

sanjay: Cost model: if we append ledger row for all requests, ingest cost moves from trace pipeline to ledger stream. We need numbers: at 1B requests/day * 120 bytes ~ 120GB/day. That's non-trivial but probably cheaper than full header explosion.

ada: I ran a small estimate using a 24h sample: moving to compact headers + ledger rows yields ~45% net reduction in trace pipeline bytes and a ~12% increase in ledger bytes. Net: ~30% total ingest savings.

leo: Operational impacts: we need a hot cache in gateway for billing_key lookups (TTL ~10s) and a graceful fallback when cache misses: either sync lookup (adds 10-20ms) or fall back to issuing a ledger row with billing_key="_pending" and enqueue an enrichment job to backfill ledger. Which do we prefer?

neha: For billing routes we should prefer sync lookups to guarantee ledger accuracy; for others, pending + backfill is OK. We must track pending ledger count.

ada: Runbook/metrics: expose `ledger_pending_count`, `ledger_write_errors`, `ledger_dedup_rate`, `gateway_billing_cache_hit_rate`, and `ledger_p99_write_latency`. Alert thresholds: pending_count > 2000 for 5m, dedup_rate > 1% for 10m.

sanjay: Query semantics: billing queries run only on ledger table; trace joins are only necessary for debugging. That simplifies analytic queries and reduces late-attr join complexity.

leo: Any security/abuse concerns? A malicious client could try to drive ledger writes. Mitigations: route_token HMAC + rate limits + enforce that gateway only emits ledger rows for validated routes.

neha: Backfill/backpressure: if ledger ingestion lags, we must degrade to marking billing routes as "sync_fallback=true" or temporarily flip those routes to full header. Also plan a budget for retrocompute if we miss windows.

ada: Sampling note: sampled full headers remain for validation only. Ledger must be authoritative for billing; do not infer billing from sampled traces.

leo: Implementation steps proposal: 1) prototype gateway ledger write and cache (staging) 2) short canary: 2% edge hosts for 48h 3) compare billing sums vs baseline (automated job) 4) evaluate ingest cost delta and ops surface 5) decide whether to make ledger default or use async enrich join.

neha: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/+/3491 (proto, tests, metric hooks).

sanjay: I'll review today. One nit: make ledger TTL configurable and add a flag to gate ledger writes per-namespace.

telemetry-bot: deploy status: ledger-writer -> green :white_check_mark:, metric: ledger_pending_count=0, gateway_billing_cache_hit_rate=97%

ada: If no major objections by EOD tomorrow I'll move forward with a small staging canary. Any blockers?

leo: No blockers from infra. Please include billing team in signoff.

neha: I'll run synthetic billing parity tests once PR lands.

sanjay: I'll draft a short roll-out runbook and emergency rollback steps.

ada: Thanks all — closing when canary completes and parity checks pass.
